title: Low gov’t pay deepens shortage of occupational, speech therapists

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Low government salaries are making it difficult to attract and retain occupational therapists and speech-language pathologists in public hospitals, worsening the shortage of professionals needed to support learners with disabilities. The Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom 2) pointed to the pay disparity as it called for a review of the entry-level salary grades of occupational therapists, physical therapists and speech therapists to bring their compensation closer to market rates. The commission is pushing for higher entry-level salaries and expanded education and training opportunities for these professionals, citing high vacancy rates in government hospitals and the limited availability […]...
